S1.title: Fact check: Joe Biden doesn't want to ban all fracking, only new permits
S1.retrieval_query: What have Joe Biden and his campaign said about banning fracking, and in what contexts and dates?

passages.P1: # Fact Check: Joe Biden wants to eliminate new fracking permits, not all fracking
passages.P2: ## The claim: Joe Biden wants to eliminate fracking
passages.P3: The claim that presidential candidate and former Vice President Joe Biden wants to eliminate fracking has been made for much of the presidential campaign.
passages.P4: This summer, it was made in a post on Facebook and is similar to an ad by America First Action, a pro-Trump Political Action Committee. It includes a video of Biden answering a question in a primary debate and a claim that Biden could cost Pennsylvania more than 600,000 jobs. The video says it is paid for by America First Action.
passages.P5: The post says, “Biden on Fracking: ‘No. We would work it out. We would make sure it’s eliminated, and no more subsidies for either one of those, period.’”
passages.P6: An email to an America First Action spokeswoman seeking information about the post did not get a response.
passages.P7: As campaigning ramped up into the fall, the claim was widely repeated across social media.
passages.P8: Fracking, also known as hydraulic fracturing, is a method of extracting natural gas from the ground. It involves a horizontal drilling process that pumps water, sand and chemicals into the ground, fracturing rocks and releasing natural gas.
passages.P9: The information about the potential job loss is similar to estimates in a report by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce’s Global Energy Institute. The report, which was released in December, estimates that a ban on fracking in 2021 would lead to the loss of 5.9 million jobs in seven states by 2025, including about 600,000 in Pennsylvania.
passages.P10: ## What did Biden say, and when?
passages.P11: The video appears to be from a July 31, 2019, debate of candidates in the Democratic presidential primaries. The reference to the potential loss of 600,000 jobs appears to be connected to a study on fracking from a U.S. Chamber of Commerce group.
passages.P12: In the video, CNN’s Dana Bash asked Biden a question, according to the network’s transcript of the debate. The exchange happened after Biden had talked about his energy plan.
passages.P13: “Just to clarify, would there be any place for fossil fuels, including coal and fracking, in a Biden administration?” Bash said.
passages.P14: “No, we would — we would work it out. We would make sure it's eliminated and no more subsidies for either one of those, either — any fossil fuel,” Biden said in response.
passages.P16: It’s unclear what Biden meant by “work it out” or when the elimination would occur, but the Biden campaign said he does not want to ban fracking. Biden’s energy plan and other comments he has made shed light on his plans.
passages.P17: Biden’s website has a lengthy description of his climate proposal, which is called “Joe’s Plan for a Clean Energy Revolution and Environmental Justice.” The plan includes a call for 100% clean energy and net-zero emissions by 2050, as well as a proposal to ban on new oil and gas permits on public lands and waters.
passages.P18: Biden echoed that position at a CNN town hall in September 2019, after saying that he doesn’t support a nationwide fracking ban. He said he wants to stop all oil and gas drilling on federal lands — the federal government doesn’t have much control over state lands.
passages.P19: “I think we should in fact be looking at what exists now and making a judgment whether or not ... those in fact that are there, those wells that are there, whether or not they are dangerous, whether or not they have already done the damage,” he said.
